scent danger: The deer raised its head and ran away, as if it could scent danger hiding in the tall grass.
那隻鹿抬起頭跑走了，彷彿牠能嗅到躲在高草叢裡的危險。
scent victory: After our team scored three goals in the first half, the fans could already scent victory.
我們的隊伍上半場進了三球後，球迷們已經嗅到勝利的味道。
scent a scandal: The reporter began asking more questions because she could scent a scandal behind the mayor's strange answers.
那位記者開始問更多問題，因為她從市長奇怪的回答背後嗅出了醜聞。
throw someone off the scent: The thief changed his clothes and took a different bus to throw the police off the scent.
小偷換了衣服並搭另一班公車，想甩開警方的追蹤。
be scheduled to begin: The concert is scheduled to begin at seven, so we should leave home by six to find parking.
音樂會預定七點開始，所以我們應該在六點前出門以便找停車位。
schedule a meeting: Could you schedule a meeting with the manager for next Monday afternoon to discuss the new plan?
你可以安排下週一下午和經理開會，討論新計畫嗎？
run behind schedule: Our flight is running behind schedule because of the storm, so we will miss our connecting flight.
因為暴風雨，我們的班機進度落後，所以我們會錯過轉機航班。
ahead of schedule: Thanks to good weather, the workers finished building the new bridge two months ahead of schedule.
多虧天氣良好，工人提前兩個月完成新橋的建造。
on schedule: Even though the traffic was heavy, the school bus arrived on schedule and nobody was late.
儘管交通繁忙，校車仍準時抵達，沒有人遲到。
scheme against someone: In the drama, the jealous prince began to scheme against his brother in order to take the throne.
在這部劇裡，善妒的王子開始密謀對付他的哥哥，想奪取王位。
scheme to get rich: The two men would secretly scheme to get rich by selling fake medicine online, until the police caught them.
那兩個男人暗中計畫靠網路賣假藥致富，直到被警方逮捕。
a get-rich-quick scheme: My uncle lost all his savings after joining a get-rich-quick scheme that promised huge profits in one month.
我叔叔參加了一個承諾一個月就獲得暴利的快速致富騙局，結果賠光了所有積蓄。
the scheme of things: Failing one quiz feels terrible now, but in the scheme of things, it is not that important.
一次小考不及格現在感覺很糟，但從整體格局來看，它並沒有那麼重要。
scold a child: It is better to explain the problem calmly than to scold a child loudly in front of others.
冷靜地說明問題，比在別人面前大聲責罵小孩更好。
be scolded for: Tom was scolded for leaving his dirty socks on the living room floor again by his angry mother.
湯姆又因把髒襪子丟在客廳地上而挨了生氣的媽媽一頓罵。
scold someone for being late: Our coach will scold anyone for being late and make them run five extra laps around the field.
我們教練會罵任何遲到的人，還要他們繞操場多跑五圈。
scoop up the ball: The shortstop ran forward to scoop up the ball with his glove and quickly threw it to first base.
游擊手往前衝，用手套撈起球，並迅速傳向一壘。
scoop the prize: Our class practiced the play for weeks, hoping to scoop the prize at the school drama contest.
我們班練了好幾週的戲，希望在校內戲劇比賽中抱走大獎。
get a scoop: The young journalist waited outside the hotel all night, hoping to get a scoop about the famous singer.
那位年輕記者在飯店外守了一整夜，希望拿到那位知名歌手的獨家新聞。
scoop ice cream: My summer job at the dessert shop is to scoop ice cream into cones for hungry customers.
我在甜點店的暑期工作是把冰淇淋挖進甜筒裡給饑餓的客人。
score a goal: In the last minute of the game, Kevin kicked the ball past the goalkeeper to score a goal.
在比賽最後一分鐘，凱文把球踢過守門員，進球得分。
score points with someone: He offered to carry the heavy boxes, hoping to score points with his new boss.
他主動幫忙搬重箱子，希望博得新老闆的好感。
score a victory: Although nobody expected much from them, the small school's team managed to score a surprising victory in the final.
雖然沒人對他們抱太大期望，這所小學校的隊伍還是在決賽中贏得了令人驚訝的勝利。
score high on the test: If you review your notes every day, you will have a better chance to score high on the test.
如果你每天複習筆記，就更有機會在考試中考高分。
settle a score: After losing to them last year, our team was eager to settle a score in this year's final.
去年輸給他們之後，我們隊急著要在今年的決賽中算舊帳。
know the score: You don't need to explain the rules again; everyone here knows the score and what will happen if we fail.
你不需要再解釋規則了；這裡每個人都清楚狀況，也知道如果失敗會怎樣。
scramble for seats: When the train doors opened, tired passengers began to scramble for seats near the windows.
火車門一打開，疲倦的乘客就開始搶靠窗的座位。
scramble to finish: With only five minutes left before the bell, the students had to scramble to finish the last questions.
離鐘響只剩五分鐘，學生們不得不趕著完成最後幾題。
scramble eggs: On Sunday mornings, my brother likes to scramble eggs with cheese and serve them with toast.
週日早上，我哥喜歡加起司炒蛋，配吐司一起吃。
scramble the signal: The army used special equipment to scramble the signal so that the enemy could not understand their messages.
軍隊使用特殊設備使訊號加密，讓敵人無法理解他們的訊息。
scramble up the hill: The kids had to scramble up the hill on their hands and knees, racing to reach the top first.
孩子們得手腳並用爬上山，比賽誰先到達山頂。
